messages.content: Find an Italian restaurant near me in New York that provides vegetarian food options and a Japanese sushi restaurant in Los Angeles that offers delivery service.

function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

message.reasoning:
We need to call two separate searches using the restaurant_finder tool.

First request: city=New York (NY), cuisine="Italian", preferences include Vegetarian? The preference list should contain "Vegetarian". Also maybe Delivery but not required; we can just specify Vegetarian.

Second request: city=Los Angeles (LA) presumably California, cuisine="Japanese", preferences includes "Delivery".

We'll produce calls accordingly.

Let's do first:

{
    location:"New York, NY",
    cuisine:"Italian",
    preferences:["Vegetarian"]
}

But note the schema says preferences optional param with union types: "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[] . Actually it's array of strings each being one of those values. So pass ["Vegetarian"].

Similarly second:

{location:"Los Angeles, CA", cuisine:"Japanese", preferences:["Delivery"] }

Return results from both calls. We'll output them as JSON or plain text? Usually assistant returns result after calling function. We might combine into single response listing both sets.

Thus we will make two function calls sequentially. Let's proceed.
